Second independent check — is this M13 finding a REAL, actionable issue to fix before merge? Read the code; be skeptical; confirm only with a concrete pointer.
File:components/admin/UsersTable.tsx (components/admin/UsersTable.tsx:64-66 (SuspendUserButton render) + components/admin/SuspendUserButton.tsx:42-49; components/admin/ReportCard.tsx:88-97)
Row action buttons have identical, ambiguous accessible names across rows
In the Users table, every row renders <SuspendUserButton> whose visible label/accessible name is just t("admin.suspend") = "Suspend" (or "Reinstate"). The user's `name` prop is passed in but only used inside the toast/announce string (SuspendUserButton.tsx:33-34) — it is never surfaced on the button itself (no aria-label / aria-describedby). So a screen-reader user navigating by buttons (or the WCAG 2.4.4 / 4.1.2 "buttons with the same name must have the same/ disambiguated purpose" expectation) hears "Suspend, button" repeated for every active user with no way to tell which user each one acts on. The same applies to ReportCard's "Mark reviewed" and "Suspend the reported user" buttons, which repeat verbatim across every report card. This is confirmed by the test (tests/component/admin-dashboard.test.tsx:65) which can only query getByRole('button',{name:/^suspend$/i}) because the fixture happens to contain exactly one suspendable active non-admin user; with two it would match multiple elements. axe does not auto-flag duplicate accessible names, so the axe assertion passes while the real ambiguity remains. Note: provider/listener dashboards (e.g. provider session links) typically carry the subject name in the control's context; this admin table does not.

content.text: I'll verify this finding by reading the relevant files.
Now let me check the `Button` component to see if it forwards `aria-label`, and verify the test claim.

The finding is confirmed in the code. Let me verify a few of the specific claims to be precise and skeptical.

Now I'll verify the WCAG framing. The finding cites WCAG 2.4.4 (Link Purpose) and 4.1.2 (Name, Role, Value). Let me check whether there's any other context that would disambiguate the buttons (e.g., DataTable wrapping with row headers / `aria` context).

I have confirmed all the load-bearing facts. Let me assess this carefully and skeptically.

**What's confirmed in the code:**

1. `UsersTable.tsx:55` renders `<SuspendUserButton userId={r.id} name={r.name} suspended={r.suspended} />` for every non-admin row.
2. `SuspendUserButton.tsx:40-48` — the `name` prop is used ONLY in the `announce()` toast string (lines 33-34). The button's accessible name is purely `t("admin.suspend")` / `t("admin.reinstate")` with no `aria-label`, `aria-describedby`, or other disambiguation. `Button` spreads `...rest` so an `aria-label` *could* be passed but isn't.
3. The cells are plain `<td>` (no `<th scope="row">` in DataTable, and even if there were, row headers don't get exposed as part of a button's accessible name without explicit association). So nothing programmatically ties the button to the user's name/email.
4. `ReportCard.tsx:83-96` — "Mark reviewed" and "Suspend the reported user" buttons repeat verbatim per card with no per-card disambiguation on the control itself.
5. The test at line 64 relies on `getByRole('button',{name:/^suspend$/i})` matching exactly one element because the fixture has exactly one active non-admin user. With two active non-admin users it would throw on multiple matches — confirming the ambiguity is real and the test only passes by fixture coincidence.

**Skeptical assessment of severity:** This is a genuine WCAG 2.4.4 / ARIA-authoring concern (ambiguous accessible names for repeated controls). axe genuinely does not flag duplicate accessible names, so the passing axe assertion does not cover it. The CLAUDE.md golden rule #1 makes accessibility "non-negotiable" and the project explicitly targets screen-reader operability. So this is in-scope and actionable, not a nitpick.

**However**, I should be honest about the nuance: a screen-reader user reading the table cell-by-cell *does* encounter the name in the row before reaching the button cell, so it is not fully "no way to tell." The real failure mode is the buttons-list / forms-list navigation mode (where context is stripped) and the WCAG 2.4.4 best-practice expectation. The finding's framing slightly overstates ("no way to tell which user") but the core issue — repeated identical accessible names on per-row/per-card destructive actions — is real and the fix (add `aria-label` like "Suspend Casey") is concrete and small.

This is a real, actionable issue worth fixing before merge.

input.reason: Confirmed real and actionable. In components/admin/UsersTable.tsx:55 every non-admin row renders <SuspendUserButton userId name suspended>, but in components/admin/SuspendUserButton.tsx:40-48 the `name` prop is used ONLY inside the announce() toast (lines 33-34); the button's accessible name is just t("admin.suspend")/t("admin.reinstate") with no aria-label/aria-describedby (Button spreads ...rest, so one could be passed but none is). DataTable renders rows as plain <td> with no row-header association, so nothing ties the control to the subject user. Result: every active user yields an identical "Suspend, button" accessible name with no programmatic disambiguation — a WCAG 2.4.4 / 4.1.2 best-practice violation that is fully exposed in buttons/forms screen-reader navigation modes. Same pattern in components/admin/ReportCard.tsx:83-96: "Mark reviewed" and "Suspend the reported user" repeat verbatim across every report card with no per-card identifier on the control. The claim that axe does not catch this is correct (axe does not flag duplicate accessible names), so the passing axe assertions give false confidence. The test at tests/component/admin-dashboard.test.tsx:64 confirms the latent ambiguity — getByRole('button',{name:/^suspend$/i}) only works because the fixture has exactly one active non-admin user; a second active user would throw a multiple-match error. Given CLAUDE.md golden rule #1 (accessibility non-negotiable, screen-reader operability), this is in scope. Concrete fix: add a per-row/per-card aria-label (e.g. t("admin.suspendUser",{name}) -> "Suspend Casey") to each control. One nuance: a SR user reading cell-by-cell does hear the name in the preceding cell, so "no way to tell" is slightly overstated — but the duplicate-accessible-name issue and the fix are real and small, so it should be fixed before merge.
